questions.passage_md:
**Books Borrowed from Riverside Library, by Format**

| Year | Print books | E-books | Audiobooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 48,000 | 12,000 | 6,000 |
| 2022 | 45,000 | 16,000 | 9,000 |
| 2023 | 44,000 | 21,000 | 13,000 |

A library volunteer notes that while print books were still the most borrowed format each year, digital formats were growing.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the volunteer’s statement?
choices: Print book borrowing fell from 48,000 in 2021 to 44,000 in 2023.
In every year, more print books than e-books or audiobooks were borrowed, and both e-book and audiobook borrowing rose each year.
Audiobooks were the least borrowed format in 2021.
E-book borrowing in 2023 was 21,000.
questions.explanation_md: The statement has two parts: print was the top format every year, and digital formats grew. Choice B covers both (print leads every year; e-books go 12k → 16k → 21k and audiobooks 6k → 9k → 13k).

distractor_notes.A: This is accurate but addresses only the decline in print, not the growth of digital formats.
distractor_notes.C: Accurate, but it shows neither print’s lead nor digital growth.
distractor_notes.D: A single number can’t show a trend of growth.

questions.passage_md:
**Average Daily High Temperature (°C) in Two Cities**

| Month | Coastal City | Inland City |
|---|---|---|
| January | 14 | 6 |
| April | 17 | 18 |
| July | 22 | 33 |
| October | 19 | 20 |

A student claims that the inland city has a wider range of temperatures over the year than the coastal city does.
questions.stem_md: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the student’s claim?
choices: In April, the inland city was 1 degree warmer than the coastal city.
The coastal city’s highest average was 22°C, in July.
The inland city’s averages range from 6°C to 33°C, a span of 27 degrees, while the coastal city’s range from 14°C to 22°C, a span of only 8 degrees.
Both cities were warmer in October than in January.
questions.explanation_md: The claim compares the *range* of temperatures in the two cities. Choice C computes both ranges (27 versus 8 degrees), which supports it directly.

distractor_notes.A: A single month’s difference says nothing about the range over the year.
distractor_notes.B: This describes only the coastal city, with no comparison.
distractor_notes.D: This is true of both cities and doesn’t compare their ranges.

questions.passage_md:
**Survey: How Students at Lakeview High Usually Get to School**

| Method | Percent of students |
|---|---|
| School bus | 38% |
| Car (driven by family) | 27% |
| Walk or bike | 22% |
| Drive themselves | 13% |

The student council wants to add bike racks, arguing that a meaningful share of students already arrive without a car or bus.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the student council’s argument?
choices: 38% of students take the school bus.
22% of students walk or bike to school.
13% of students drive themselves.
27% of students are driven by family members.
questions.explanation_md: The argument is about students who come without a car or bus. Walking or biking (22%) is that group.

distractor_notes.A: Bus riders are the group the argument sets aside.
distractor_notes.C: Students who drive themselves arrive by car.
distractor_notes.D: Students driven by family arrive by car.

questions.passage_md:
**Monarch Butterflies Counted at a Garden, by Week**

| Week | Monarchs counted |
|---|---|
| 1 | 4 |
| 2 | 11 |
| 3 | 26 |
| 4 | 19 |
| 5 | 7 |

A gardener observed that the number of monarchs peaked in the middle of the five-week period.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the gardener’s observation?
choices: The count rose from 4 in week 1 to a high of 26 in week 3, then fell to 7 by week 5.
The count in week 5 was greater than the count in week 1.
The count in week 2 was 11.
More monarchs were counted in week 4 than in week 2.
questions.explanation_md: A peak in the middle means the counts rise, reach their highest point near week 3, then fall. Choice A describes that shape.

distractor_notes.B: Comparing only the endpoints says nothing about a peak in the middle.
distractor_notes.C: A single week’s count can’t show a peak.
distractor_notes.D: True, but it doesn’t show that the highest count was in the middle.

questions.passage_md:
**Germination Rate of Tomato Seeds at Different Soil Temperatures**

| Soil temperature | Seeds planted | Seeds germinated |
|---|---|---|
| 10°C | 200 | 34 |
| 18°C | 200 | 142 |
| 25°C | 200 | 181 |
| 32°C | 200 | 120 |

A horticulturist concludes that tomato seeds germinate best at moderately warm temperatures and that both cooler and hotter soil reduce germination.
questions.stem_md: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the horticulturist’s conclusion?
choices: At 18°C, 142 of 200 seeds germinated.
More seeds germinated at 32°C than at 10°C.
Germination was highest at 25°C (181 of 200 seeds) and lower both at 18°C and below and at 32°C (120 of 200 seeds).
Every temperature tested had at least some seeds germinate.
questions.explanation_md: The conclusion has three parts: a best (moderate) temperature, lower germination when cooler, and lower germination when hotter. Choice C shows the peak at 25°C with drops on both sides.

distractor_notes.A: One data point can’t show where the peak is or that hotter soil hurts germination.
distractor_notes.B: This compares the two extremes and ignores the peak.
distractor_notes.D: This is true but doesn’t address which temperature is best.

questions.passage_md:
**Share of Electricity Generated from Wind, by Region**

| Region | 2015 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|
| North | 8% | 21% |
| South | 12% | 15% |
| East | 5% | 9% |
| West | 15% | 18% |

An energy analyst argues that although the West had the largest share of wind power in 2015, the North showed by far the fastest growth over the period.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the analyst’s argument?
choices: The West’s share rose from 15% to 18%, while the North’s share rose from 8% to 21%, an increase of 13 percentage points compared with increases of 3 to 4 points in the other regions.
The South’s share of wind power was greater than the East’s in both years.
In 2020, the North had a larger share of wind power than any other region.
The East had the smallest share of wind power in both 2015 and 2020.
questions.explanation_md: The argument makes two points: the West led in 2015 (15%), and the North grew fastest. Choice A notes the West’s 2015 figure and shows the North’s 13-point rise compared with 3–4 points elsewhere.

distractor_notes.B: This compares two regions the argument doesn’t mention.
distractor_notes.C: The North’s 2020 lead is a level, not a growth rate, and it leaves out the West’s 2015 lead.
distractor_notes.D: The East isn’t part of the argument.

questions.passage_md:
**Average Minutes of Homework per Night, by Grade and Semester**

| Grade | Fall | Spring |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 52 | 58 |
| 10 | 61 | 64 |
| 11 | 75 | 92 |
| 12 | 70 | 55 |

A school counselor notes that homework time increased from fall to spring in every grade except one.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the counselor’s statement?
choices: Grade 11 students did the most homework in the spring.
Homework time rose from fall to spring in grades 9, 10, and 11, but fell in grade 12, from 70 to 55 minutes.
Grade 9 students did the least homework in the fall.
Grade 12 students did 70 minutes of homework per night in the fall.
questions.explanation_md: The statement says time rose in every grade *except one*. Choice B shows the rise in three grades and names the exception (grade 12).

distractor_notes.A: This is true, but it doesn’t describe the change from fall to spring across grades.
distractor_notes.C: This describes a single grade in a single semester.
distractor_notes.D: This gives one number without showing any change.

questions.passage_md:
Researchers compared two methods of teaching fractions to fourth graders. Students took the same test before and after a six-week unit.

| Method | Average pretest score | Average posttest score |
|---|---|---|
| Number-line lessons | 54 | 78 |
| Worksheet practice | 55 | 66 |

The researchers concluded that the number-line lessons were more effective than worksheet practice.
questions.stem_md: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researchers’ conclusion?
choices: Students using worksheet practice started with a slightly higher average score than students using number-line lessons.
Both groups had higher average scores after the unit than before it.
Although the two groups started with nearly the same average scores (54 and 55), the number-line group improved by 24 points, while the worksheet group improved by only 11.
The worksheet group’s average posttest score was 66.
questions.explanation_md: To show one method worked better, compare improvement between groups that started out equal. Choice C notes the similar starting scores and the larger gain for number lines (24 versus 11 points).

distractor_notes.A: Starting scores alone don’t show which method was more effective.
distractor_notes.B: Both groups improved, so this doesn’t favor either method.
distractor_notes.D: A single number with no comparison can’t support the conclusion.

questions.passage_md:
Ecologists measured how many seeds of two plant species were carried away by ants and by rodents in a forest over one month.

| Species | Seeds removed by ants | Seeds removed by rodents | Seeds not removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wild ginger | 310 | 45 | 145 |
| Trillium | 190 | 60 | 250 |

(500 seeds of each species were set out.)

The ecologists hypothesized that wild ginger relies more heavily on ants to spread its seeds than trillium does.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the ecologists’ hypothesis?
choices: Rodents removed more trillium seeds than wild ginger seeds.
Ants removed 62% of wild ginger seeds (310 of 500) but only 38% of trillium seeds (190 of 500).
More trillium seeds than wild ginger seeds were not removed at all.
Ants removed more seeds than rodents did for both species.
questions.explanation_md: The hypothesis compares how much each species depends on ants. Choice B compares the share of seeds ants removed: 62% for wild ginger versus 38% for trillium.

distractor_notes.A: This is about rodents, not ants.
distractor_notes.C: Seeds left in place don’t directly show reliance on ants.
distractor_notes.D: True for both species, so it doesn’t show that wild ginger relies on ants *more*.

questions.passage_md:
**Visitors to Three State Parks (thousands)**

| Park | 2019 | 2021 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pine Ridge | 420 | 610 | 540 |
| Cedar Falls | 380 | 395 | 410 |
| Blue Lake | 510 | 700 | 450 |

A tourism official claims that one park’s attendance grew steadily over the whole period, while the other two rose sharply and then declined.
questions.stem_md: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the official’s claim?
choices: Blue Lake had the most visitors in 2019 and 2021.
Pine Ridge and Blue Lake both had more visitors in 2021 than in 2019.
Cedar Falls rose from 380 to 395 to 410 thousand visitors, while Pine Ridge and Blue Lake peaked in 2021 (at 610 and 700 thousand) and then fell by 2023.
Blue Lake had fewer visitors in 2023 than in 2019.
questions.explanation_md: The claim contrasts one park with steady growth against two that peaked and then declined. Choice C describes both patterns with the right parks.

distractor_notes.A: This ranks parks by size but says nothing about trends.
distractor_notes.B: This shows the rise but not the later decline, and it leaves out Cedar Falls’ steady growth.
distractor_notes.D: This covers only one park, and only its endpoints.

questions.passage_md:
A company tested whether a four-day workweek affected output. Two similar teams were compared over six months.

| Team | Schedule | Projects completed | Sick days taken |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 4 days (32 hours) | 46 | 18 |
| B | 5 days (40 hours) | 45 | 31 |

A manager argues that the shorter week did not reduce productivity and may have improved employee health.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the manager’s argument?
choices: Team A worked 8 fewer hours per week than Team B.
Team B completed 45 projects in six months.
Team A completed about as many projects as Team B (46 versus 45) and took fewer sick days (18 versus 31).
Team B took 31 sick days, more than any other team in the company.
questions.explanation_md: The argument has two parts: productivity held steady (46 versus 45 projects) and health may have improved (18 versus 31 sick days). Choice C covers both.

distractor_notes.A: This describes the schedules, not their results.
distractor_notes.B: This gives one team’s output with no comparison.
distractor_notes.D: The table shows only two teams, so there is no data about “any other team.”

questions.passage_md:
**Share of Adults Who Read at Least One Book in the Past Year, by Age Group**

| Age group | Print only | Digital only | Both print and digital |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18–29 | 22% | 14% | 44% |
| 30–49 | 30% | 9% | 35% |
| 50–64 | 38% | 6% | 24% |
| 65+ | 45% | 3% | 16% |

A researcher states that younger adults were more likely than older adults to read in more than one format.
questions.stem_md: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researcher’s statement?
choices: The share of adults who read print only rose from 22% among 18–29-year-olds to 45% among those 65 and older.
Adults aged 18–29 were the most likely to read digital only.
The share who read both print and digital fell steadily with age, from 44% of 18–29-year-olds to 16% of those 65 and older.
Among adults 65 and older, 3% read digital only.
questions.explanation_md: “More than one format” means the “Both print and digital” column. Choice C shows that share falling steadily from the youngest group to the oldest.

distractor_notes.A: Print-only readers use a single format.
distractor_notes.B: Digital-only readers also use a single format.
distractor_notes.D: This describes one group, for a single format.
